newsitem.title: GERMANY: Investment in east Germany drops 5 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Investment in east Germany drops 5 pct in 96.

text.p: One of Germany's leading economic think-tanks said on Thursday that investment in east Germany fell five percent in 1996 from the year before as investment begins to fall from high levels following German unification.

Although investment trends were clearly normalising after the post-unification flood of capital into the former communist region, investment per employee remains twice as high as in the affluent west German states.
The Munich-based Ifo economic research institute said in a report that investment in east Germany totalled 17.5 billion marks this year, down five percent from a post-unification high in 1995.
The report said the lion's share of the east German investment this year was made in the steel and iron making sectors as well as the chemical and wood processing industries.
Investment in urban trains increased after a lean period, while shipbuilding investment was down.
Investment in construction fell to 25 percent of the total for 1996 from 30 percent the year before. A steeper decline was offset by a rise in foreign investment.
